# Finding the Largest Gap Between Per-Layer and Per-Output Perplexity

## Analysis

Looking at the figure, I need to compare the Per-Output (blue) and Per-Layer (orange) bars at each sparsity rate. Since the y-axis is on a logarithmic scale, I need to consider the absolute differences carefully.

Let me examine the values at each sparsity rate:

| Sparsity Rate | Per-Output (blue) | Per-Layer (orange) | Approximate Gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10% | ~5 | ~5 | negligible |
| 20% | ~5 | ~5 | negligible |
| 30% | ~5 | ~5.5 | very small |
| 40% | ~6 | ~6.5 | small |
| 50% | ~7 | ~8 | small |
| 60% | ~10 | ~12 | moderate |
| 70% | ~20 | ~35 | ~15 |
| 80% | ~500 | ~900 | ~400 |

## Conclusion

The largest gap between Per-Layer and Per-Output perplexity occurs at **80% sparsity rate**. At this point, the Per-Output perplexity is approximately 500 while the Per-Layer perplexity reaches approximately 900, creating a difference of roughly 400 — by far the largest absolute gap between the two methods. This makes intuitive sense, as extreme sparsity levels amplify the differences between pruning granularities.
